messages.subject: Re: CODEX & Ion Torrent Data
parts:
Hi Taylor,

Thanks for your interest in CODEX. I’ve never personally applied CODEX to WES data from the Ion Torrent platform but I assume GC content, capture and amplification biases, as well as latent artifacts also apply to and are mixed in the Torrent data. In this case, you can certainly apply CODEX to call CNVs. I am very interested in how CODEX works and please keep me updated and let me know if you’ve encountered any questions. Make sure that you have the most updated version of CODEX. You can use the command below in R to re-install:

install.packages("devtools"); library(devtools); install_github("yuchaojiang/CODEX/package")

I am cc’ing our mailing list in case other users have similar questions.

Cheers,
Yuchao


On May 13, 2016, at 11:31 AM, MacIsaac, Taylor <Taylor....@phri.ca> wrote:

Hi Yuchao,

My Name is Taylor MacIsaac, I am contacting you on behalf of the Population Health Research Institute in Ontario, Canada. I am working on a project analyzing WES data generated from the Ion Torrent platform and I am wondering if CONDEX has successfully been used to call CNV’s with Torrent data?

Thanks very much for any assistance you can provide,
